walkthroughs.body_html:
The Origins & Course of the First World War 1905-18 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Origins & Course of the First World War 1905-18 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: How many British casualties on first day of Somme?
Why did the League of Nations fail to prevent WWII?
options: The Schlieffen Plan failed because it tried to invade Russia first.
The League failed because no countries joined it.
The League failed because Hitler banned it in 1933.
Absence of the US, requirement of unanimous decisions, no armed force of its own, weak responses to Manchuria (1931) and Abyssinia (1935), and great-power self-interest.

mcqs.q: Why did the Schlieffen Plan fail in 1914?
options: The Schlieffen Plan failed because it tried to invade Russia first.
Belgian resistance delayed the German advance; Russia mobilised faster than expected; Moltke weakened the right wing; and the French rallied at the Marne.
The Schlieffen Plan failed because Britain entered the war.
The League failed because Hitler banned it in 1933.
